items.q: Why do kind people freeze at the edge of a conversation they don't know?
items.a: They treat **contribution as expert knowledge**, then wait for a gap that never comes. Vinh splits it: **enter the circle**, and **add value without topic mastery**.
Over-considerate people **mute visual and vocal signals**, so the room assumes they do not want in. Intent stays trapped in the brain. "People can't see inside of your brain."

items.q: How can a question count as a contribution?
items.a: "**How did you find this?**" or "**What sparked your interest?**" opens their story (dad, teacher, first memory) and gives you a **bridge** into your own. Quantum physics still works: ask what started it, then "tell me more."

items.q: What should you signal before you have content?
items.a: **"Ah" plus a look or lean** so the group can invite you. Then play — a cheeky "how is this only my first time?" Start with **2–3 jumps**, not fifty.

items.q: What is the lunch/meeting rule so you never leave invisible?
items.a: At least **one question**, **one contribution**, visible **once** (ideally **1–3 times**) every gathering. Enough asks and other considerate people fire one back — that is your talk slot.
